subject: Security questionnaire: region-lock erasure, TTL, and backup eviction (Hosted API)
messages:
From: Martin Cole <security@abendtech.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Region-lock erasure & retention details for Hosted API (security questionnaire)

Hi Jonas,

We're finishing our vendor assessment and had a few specific questions on how Redwood treats customer data for the Hosted API when customers require EU-only residency and fast erasure. I've attached our questionnaire (ab_security_questionnaire_v3.pdf) and highlighted the questions that matter most:

1) Can you confirm whether request/response payloads and derived artifacts (embeddings, reranks, persist caches) can be pinned to a single EU region and remain within that region at rest?

2) What are the out-of-the-box retention TTLs for request payloads, logs, model caches, and search indexes? Are these configurable per-tenant at provisioning time?

3) If AbendTech issues a customer-initiated erasure (subject access / right to be forgotten), what are the exact semantics:
   - Is there a soft-delete (tombstone) followed by a hard-delete?
   - What windows apply to primary storage vs. backups/snapshots?
   - How do you provide proof of deletion / attestation?

4) How are backups and point-in-time snapshots handled for hosted tenants in EU regions? Are snapshot copies replicated outside of EU for DR? If so, what controls exist?

5) For hosted customers, what key management options exist (AWS-managed KMS vs customer-managed keys)? How does that affect ability to destroy keys and render archived backups unreadable?

We also need a short, plain-language statement we can include in our risk register and evidence we can attach to our SOC/infosec packet.

Can you respond in-line to the attached questionnaire, or send a consolidated reply? We may ask for a short call to go through the deletion timeline.

Thanks,
Martin Cole
Head of Security, AbendTech
security@abendtech.com

Attachment: ab_security_questionnaire_v3.pdf (pdf - 94KB, answered rows highlighted)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Region-lock erasure & retention details for Hosted API (security questionnaire)

Martin — thanks for the detailed questions and the questionnaire. Inline answers below (consolidated for clarity). Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you'd like to walk through the timeline and evidence samples.

Summary (tl;dr):
- Hosted API supports region-bound data storage for request/response payloads and derived artifacts when the project is provisioned in an EU region. Control plane metadata required for routing is minimized and retained only for operational troubleshooting (see note).
- Default retention: request payloads (30 days), logs (90 days), model cache/KV (ephemeral by default; 24-72 hrs), embeddings/derived indexes (30 days). All values are configurable per-tenant at provisioning for Hosted customers, within policy limits (0 = ephemeral to 365 days).
- Erasure semantics: we implement a two-phase process: 1) immediate logical tombstone (marked) and removal from live indexes; 2) background physical purge from primary storage within 72 hours. Backups/snapshots are on a scheduled sweep and reconciled within 30 days; final irrevocable removal from immutable backup copies occurs during the next backup retention cycle (up to 30 days).
- Backups/snapshots: For EU-hosted projects, snapshots are stored in-region by default. We do not replicate snapshots outside the EU for Hosted EU projects unless the customer opts into cross-region DR. Customer requests for EU-only guarantees are captured in the provisioning settings and contract addendum.
- Key management: Hosted uses cloud-provider managed KMS (AWS KMS / Google Cloud KMS) by default. Customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) is available on Dedicated and Private plans; for Hosted we can offer a dedicated CMK under an enterprise addendum (subject to legal/contract). Key destruction for hosted-managed keys follows provider timelines and will render encrypted backups unreadable once destroyed; please see our KMS note below.

Details / itemized answers:
1) Region-binding: when you choose an EU project during onboarding we allocate compute + storage in eu-west-1 (or chosen EU region). Request/response payloads, embeddings, and derived indexes created by that project are persisted to region-local object stores and block volumes. Minimal routing metadata (tenant id, region tag, request timestamps) is stored in the control plane for orchestration; that metadata does not contain PII and can be redacted on request.

2) Retention defaults & configurability:
   - Request payloads (user input & generated outputs): default 30 days, configurable 0–365 days at project level.
   - Embeddings & derived artifacts: default 30 days, configurable 0–365 days.
   - Model cache / per-request KV: ephemeral; default eviction 24–72 hours depending on workload.
   - System logs (audit + infra logs): default 90 days; longer retention available by contract.

3) Erasure process (customer-initiated):
   - Step A — Tombstone: we mark matching records as deleted immediately and remove entries from live search indexes in under 5 minutes.
   - Step B — Primary purge: asynchronous worker purges physical objects from primary storage within 72 hours.
   - Step C — Backup sweep: snapshot and backup reconciliation removes references during the next cleanup cycle; final removal from immutable snapshots can take up to 30 days. For customers requiring shorter backup eviction windows we offer a contractual SLA on Dedicated/Private deployments.

4) Backups & cross-region replication:
   - Default: backups for EU projects are kept in-region.
   - Cross-region replication: not performed for EU-hosted projects unless explicitly enabled for DR; this is an opt-in and captured in provisioning.

5) KMS & key destroy:
   - Hosted (default): cloud-provider-managed KMS. Key destruction is handled per provider policy; destroying a key renders encrypted snapshots unreadable.
   - Enterprise option: dedicated CMK for Hosted where we can coordinate a key lifecycle model. For Dedicated/Private customers we support full BYOK/HSM integrations.

Evidence and attestation:
- We can supply: (a) redacted data-flow diagram (attached), (b) retention_matrix_v2.pdf showing configurable TTLs, and (c) a deletion attestation template (signed statement with timestamp and job ids) after we execute a scheduled purge.
- Our SOC 2 report is available at: https://redwood.example.com/soc2-report/2026. We can provide a short attestation on deletion events including job ids and object manifests (redacted).

Caveats & notes:
- Very short backup eviction windows (<7 days) for hosted customers require a contractual commitment and a runbook that may affect recoverability/DR.
- Control-plane telemetry used for routing does include operational metadata; if AbendTech requires that to be stripped we can add that to the provisioning checklist (will require Signed MSA addendum).

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, we can provide a formal attestation template and a sample deletion event report.
2) Optional 30-minute call to walk through timelines and to lock the provisioning flags for EU-only hosting and backup policies.

Attachments: redwood_data_flow_diagram.png (png - 1.2MB), retention_matrix_v2.pdf (pdf - 220KB)

Regards,
